criteria.summary: Efficiency: both runs assessed (not partial) with at least 2 distinct explained commands and high scan efficiency confidence; a change of 15 or more points is labeled. Latency: at least 30 operations in both runs; the full-run average must move by at least 1 ms and 20%, and a p95 from at least 20 retained samples on both sides must not move materially the other way. Impact: at least 30 operations and complete impact group coverage in both runs; the share of observed operation time must move by at least 5 percentage points and 25%. Unpinned baselines older than 30 days are outdated; pinned reference runs never are.

Efficiency evidence is at most 2 explained representative commands per shape per run, chosen from retained samples; it is not a statistical sample of the shape's operations.
Only full-run sums are kept for latency, so there is no variance estimate; latency labels are a magnitude rule, not a statistical test.
Data distribution, collection size, cache state, and load from other clients are not recorded; any of them can change these metrics without an annotation.

History keeps one snapshot per shape per run for the newest 5 unpinned runs plus up to 10 pinned reference runs. With the previous-run comparison, latency and impact use the newest compatible earlier snapshot, and efficiency prefers the newest compatible snapshot with assessed evidence, so the two can come from different runs.
Topology comes from the explain layout: mongod means a mongod answered directly (standalone or replica-set member, not distinguished); sharded_cluster means a mongos layout.
view.method_note: Each tracked shape is compared with its stored snapshot from an earlier run, matched by shape id and namespace. By default the baseline is the previous compatible run: for each shape and metric, the newest earlier snapshot that passes the compatibility gates (efficiency prefers assessed evidence). A chosen run or pinned reference run is used for every shape instead. Scan efficiency score, latency (full-run average), and workload impact (share of observed operation time) are compared separately and are never combined. A label is given only when the baseline is compatible (same shape identity and score version, not outdated) and both runs meet the evidence minimums; otherwise the state says why there is no label.

notes: Measured by re-running each representative command with explain executionStats after the workload, not during the original operations; values describe that explain run only.
Sort bytes processed (totalDataSizeSorted, or totalDataSizeSortedBytesEstimate for a $sort pipeline stage) is the amount of data the sort handled, not its peak memory.

Memory limit (memLimit) is the stage's in-memory limit before it must spill, not memory used. Peak memory is shown only when a stage reports it (maxMemoryUsageBytes, memUsage, or maxAccumulatorMemoryUsageBytes per accumulator).

Spilled data size (spilledBytes, or numBytesSpilledEstimate for classic $group) is the server's size of the records it wrote to temporary files; spill file size (spilledDataStorageSize) is the storage those files used. Neither is peak memory, and they are not interchangeable.

On MongoDB 7.0 and 8.0 the slot-based sort counts totalDataSizeSorted only for data it spilled, so a 0 from a sort that did not spill and returned rows is shown as "reported value unreliable", not as no sort work. "Not reported" means the field was absent. Every other reported 0 is shown as 0. After a spill the field is shown as reported; by the server source it leaves out the last in-memory run (not measured).
Each representative sample is shown separately; values are never averaged across samples.
Stage time (executionTimeMillisEstimate) is the server's estimate for the stage including its input stages; it is not exclusive sort time and is never summed across stages.
CPU time, lock waits, and network time are not measured.

criteria.note: These thresholds are PLGM heuristics set on synthetic fixtures. They are not statistical significance tests and have not been calibrated against real customer workloads.
criteria.summary: Efficiency: both runs assessed (not partial) with at least 2 distinct explained commands and high scan efficiency confidence; a change of 15 or more points is labeled. Latency: at least 30 operations in both runs; the full-run average must move by at least 1 ms and 20%, and a p95 from at least 20 retained samples on both sides must not move materially the other way. Impact: at least 30 operations and complete impact group coverage in both runs; the share of observed operation time must move by at least 5 percentage points and 25%. Unpinned baselines older than 30 days are outdated; pinned reference runs never are.

trends.evidence_note: Operation counts and average latency cover every completed operation of the run. p95 uses retained latency samples only. Efficiency uses the distinct explained representative commands (at most 2 per shape); a large operation count does not add explain evidence.
limitations: These thresholds are PLGM heuristics set on synthetic fixtures. They are not statistical significance tests and have not been calibrated against real customer workloads.
Efficiency evidence is at most 2 explained representative commands per shape per run, chosen from retained samples; it is not a statistical sample of the shape's operations.
Only full-run sums are kept for latency, so there is no variance estimate; latency labels are a magnitude rule, not a statistical test.
Data distribution, collection size, cache state, and load from other clients are not recorded; any of them can change these metrics without an annotation.

History keeps one snapshot per shape per run for the newest 5 unpinned runs plus up to 10 pinned reference runs. With the previous-run comparison, latency and impact use the newest compatible earlier snapshot, and efficiency prefers the newest compatible snapshot with assessed evidence, so the two can come from different runs.
Topology comes from the explain layout: mongod means a mongod answered directly (standalone or replica-set member, not distinguished); sharded_cluster means a mongos layout.
trends.method_note: Each tracked shape is compared with its stored snapshot from an earlier run, matched by shape id and namespace. By default the baseline is the previous compatible run: for each shape and metric, the newest earlier snapshot that passes the compatibility gates (efficiency prefers assessed evidence). A chosen run or pinned reference run is used for every shape instead. Scan efficiency score, latency (full-run average), and workload impact (share of observed operation time) are compared separately and are never combined. A label is given only when the baseline is compatible (same shape identity and score version, not outdated) and both runs meet the evidence minimums; otherwise the state says why there is no label.
